questions.question:
D1 — What kind of developer product is this plan shipping?
Project/branch/task: main branch, DX review of plan.md ("developer-friendly pricing tier" with a `mytool pricing` CLI command and setup wizard).
ELI10: A DX review only makes sense if we agree on what developers actually touch. This plan mixes a billing change (Stripe tier, Postgres entitlements, Redis cache, upgrade endpoint) with a small CLI surface (`mytool pricing` plus a setup wizard). The classification decides which personas I offer next, which competitors I benchmark against, and what "time to hello world" even means here.
Stakes if we pick wrong: I benchmark the wrong thing. Treating this as a CLI when the real friction is signup and billing (or the reverse) produces scores and fixes aimed at a surface developers never see.
Recommendation: A because the only surface a developer directly operates in this plan is the `mytool pricing` command and wizard; everything else is backend plumbing behind it.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Pros / cons:
A) CLI Tool (recommended)
  ✅ Matches the one concrete developer touchpoint the plan names: `mytool pricing` and the setup wizard
  ✅ Gives the review a measurable hello-world path: install, run the command, see the tier, upgrade
  ❌ Underweights the signup, checkout, and entitlement flow where the plan's own goal (more signups) lives
B) Platform / hosted service
  ✅ Centers the review on account creation, billing, and entitlement checks, which is where signups are won or lost
  ✅ Surfaces the missing auth check on the upgrade endpoint as a credibility and trust issue early
  ❌ The plan describes almost none of this surface, so the review would be scoring guesses rather than the written plan
C) Both: CLI primary, Platform secondary
  ✅ Keeps the CLI hello-world path as the spine while still auditing the upgrade and entitlement flow behind it
  ✅ Lets the persona step offer both CLI-first and evaluator personas instead of forcing one
  ❌ Roughly doubles the passes and benchmarks (human: ~1 extra hour / CC: ~5 extra min) for a plan this thin
D) No developer-facing surface, exit and use /plan-eng-review
  ✅ Honest if `mytool pricing` is a stub and the real work is a billing backend with no DX to review
  ✅ Routes the untested, unauthenticated upgrade endpoint to the review that will actually catch it
  ❌ Abandons the CLI command and wizard, which are exactly the parts a DX review exists to sharpen
Net: We are trading a focused review of the one written developer surface against a broader review of the billing flow the plan barely describes. <gstack-qid:plan-devex-review-product-type>
